description: Excavate blocks in the range and apply tractions on the face of the excavation to prevent large, instantaneous force changes. The tractions are then gradually reduced according to the keywords below. The following should be noted before using the block relax command: Live 3DEC 9.7.47 semantics: 'linear <i>' / 'nonlinear <i>' take the step count directly and EXECUTE immediately (blocks are excavated and one calculation step runs); at least one of a step count (via linear/nonlinear), table or fish must be specified or the engine rejects with 'Step, table or fish must be specified'. Keyword ORDER matters: the step spec must come first and 'minimium' after it — 'block relax linear 10 minimium 0.5' parses and executes, while 'block relax minimium 0.5 linear 10' is rejected with the step/table/fish error. Note the official 9.7 page (and this file) spell 'minimium' as the official docs do - that spelling is the official one. The 'table' form is a MODIFIER, not a step spec by itself: 'block relax table <name>' alone is rejected with the same step/table/fish error (quoted, unquoted and integer forms all tried, table existing), while 'block relax linear <n> table <name>' parses and executes; 'fish <fn>' IS valid alone (executes: excavation + step). Live 9.7.47.

keywords.name: fish
keywords.description: Specify the name of a FISH function used to reduce the applied forces. The result of the function is multiplied by the initial forces every calculation step. The function must return a value between 0 and 1.

keywords.name: linear
keywords.description: Reduce the tractions linearly to the specified minimum over the next i calculation steps.

keywords.name: nonlinear
keywords.description: Reduce the tractions non-linearly to the specified minimum over the next i calculation steps, so that the forces are initially reduced quite quickly, and then more slowly as time progresses and confinement reduces. The equation for non-linear force application is: where \(f\) is the factor multiplied by the initial forces (between 0 and 1), \(cyc\) is the number of cycles since the block relax command was issued, and \(i\) is the number of steps specified above. This equation is for a minimum of 0. For a minimum greater than 0, the force is scaled by multiplying the above equation by (1- \(min\) ) and adding \(min\) , where \(min\) is the minimum value between 0 and 1 specified with the keyword minimum (default is 0). This function approaches the specified minimum asymptotically, so the value of \(f\) does not decrease exactly to 0 over \(i\) steps. keywords.name: minimium
keywords.description: The applied forces are reduced by a factor of f . f must be between 0 and 1. If a minimum is not specified, then this defaults to 0. Must FOLLOW the step spec (linear/nonlinear/table/fish); giving minimium first is rejected with 'Step, table or fish must be specified' (live 9.7.47).

keywords.name: delete
keywords.description: Delete an existing relax condition (applied forces will be set to 0).

keywords.name: face-group
keywords.description: When a block relax command is given, all faces in the range are automatically assigned a group name. By default, the group name is relax in the slot relax . It is possible to overwrite this default by assigning a specific group name (and, optionally, slot) to the faces in the range. Note that if a group name is chosen that already exists, the string _1 will be appended to the specified group name.

keywords.name: table
keywords.description: Reduce the applied forces according to a table of (step, factor) pairs. Live 9.7.47: NOT valid alone despite the engine's 'Step, table or fish must be specified' message - must be combined with a step spec, e.g. 'block relax linear <n> table <name>'.

figure_reference.note: This command embeds reference figures that are not captured in this text corpus. Figures are PNGs under <doc-root>/_images/ (doc-root sits beside the engine install, e.g. C:/Program Files/Itasca/<product>/exe64/doc); read them directly.
